content:
maria: Posting an odd one — on Dedicated pools we're seeing KV cache resident memory steadily climb during long-context tests (~40k tokens) until eviction/spill, whereas Hosted stays flat for the same workload. Repro steps attached, can anyone sanity-check?
kevin: @maria saw similar in a perf run a few weeks ago. Suspect page alignment+network path differences (VPC MTU) change buffer registration behavior. worth checking pagefaults. :thinking_face:
sachin: I ran a quick profiler against dedicated pool-3, here's the trimmed output + command I used:
```
$ ./bin/kv_profiler --target=dedicated --model=gptx --seq=40000 --concurrency=4 
kv_cache.resident=12.8GB
kv_cache.pages_total=14520
kv_cache.pages_frag_percent=29
kv_cache.evictions=378
kv_cache.eviction_spills=124
```
Also ran `perf record -e page-faults` and saw a spike during the token churn window.
eve: Not surprising. On our on-prem racks the allocator config differs (jemalloc vs tcmalloc on hosted). Allocator arenas + hugepage flags can make reuse fail and increase fragmentation. We had luck setting `MALLOC_CONF=lg_dirty_mult:0,oversize_threshold:1` on one cluster.
maria: Hosted images have baked hugepage + kernel tunables (`transparent_hugepage=never`, `vm.swappiness=10`) by default. Dedicated AMIs might be missing those. Can someone grab /proc/meminfo + dmesg from a failing node?
kevin: I checked infra logs — a subset of customer VPCs have MTU=1400 (instead of 9000). Small MTU could lead to different RDMA scatter/gather and more frequent pinned buffer churn when using GPUDirect. Not proven but plausible. I'll validate NIC stats.
sachin: More logs from the run: eviction path shows lots of small freelist allocations failing to get contiguous frames causing spill-to-disk: 
```
kv_cache:evict=on_reuse_fail count=342 latency_ms=3.2
kv_cache:spill_to_disk=true reason="fragmented_alloc"
malloc: arena0_dirty=1.2GB arena1_dirty=900MB
```
We also saw `madvise` calls that suggest transparent hugepage interactions.
maria: Proposed action items:
- add verbose kv page layout dump at startup to collect contiguous frame maps
- run jemalloc config sweep on Dedicated and on-prem images
- infra: test MTU=9000 vs 1400 in staging for a Dedicated pool
- bake hugepage + vm tunables into Dedicated AMI
Who can own what?
eve: I can own jemalloc + on-prem sweep. I'll run two racks and one Dedicated pool and report back with fragmentation delta.
kevin: I'll own the MTU tests and NIC driver stats capture. Need a canary window — prefer overnight low-traffic.
maria: I'll open a perf ticket, add a synthetic long-context benchmark to eng-runtime perf suite, and add the kv page layout dump to the debug flags. @sachin can you upload the full profile tarball?
deploy-bot: Alert: perf-regression-detected on dedicated-gpu-pool-3: kv-cache-resident +23% over baseline. See /ops/alerts/1876543180
sachin: Uploaded tarball to s3 and linked the alert: s3://redwood-perf/kv-1876543210.tar.gz
maria: SG — will triage tomorrow morning. Temporarily lowering soft eviction cap in staging: `kv_cache.eviction.soft_limit=12G` to reduce spill while we debug. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
